verdict.scope: Consumer-reachable ERR surface (B10-ERR-1/2/3: raise/queue, ERR_error_string/ERR_error_string_n, ERR_get_error/peek) on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu at HEAD f152e82c4, exercised through the C ABI and the focused unit tests. This is NOT a discharge of the full ERR mechanism and NOT a SAFE_COMPATIBLE promotion.
verdict.summary: The controls reproduce and NEO-ERR-1/2/5/7 are repaired. NEO-ERR-3/4 are accepted as external C object/ABI contracts for C-valid states. NEO-ERR-6 is repaired at the four allocator entry points but the safe-interface gap is NOT closed: safe in-crate helpers still forward an unconstrained raw `file` to the allocator and can reach c_strlen on the failure path. That violates AGENTS.md section 7 criterion 3, so the mechanism is INDEPENDENTLY_CHECKED but not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.

take_data_invariant.slot_states: err_data is NULL, or a borrowed pointer with flags lacking ERR_TXT_MALLOCED, or a seam block with ERR_TXT_MALLOCED and err_data_size = strlen+1 (finish_data enforces nonzero extent).
returns: NULL for an empty slot or a borrowed slot whose recorded extent is 0.
the original pointer, ownership transferred, for a MALLOCED slot (always a seam block per ERR_set_error_data's contract).
a fresh slot_buf_alloc(p_size) copy for a borrowed slot with a positive extent; copy_nonoverlapping of p_size bytes, original untouched.
take_data_invariant.conclusion: After the call the result is NULL or the base of one whole seam block owned by the caller. The C adapter's unconditional CRYPTO_realloc is therefore sound for every slot shape. The only production caller is err_variadic.c:145; the other references are the declaration, documentation, and tests. No path hands a borrowed pointer to CRYPTO_realloc.
take_data_invariant.residual: A MALLOCED slot whose pointer is not a seam block would still be reallocated; that is an ERR_set_error_data external-ABI contract violation, not reachable through a C-valid object.

raise_site_closure.method: rg match counts over src/**/*.rs; each function definition matches its own call pattern, so call sites are matches minus one.
raise_site_closure.static_sites: ErrSite is pub(crate), holds &'static CStr fields, and every construction uses FILE (a &'static CStr) or a c"..." literal. No ErrSite is built from a runtime pointer; inline constructions (cmp_genm, cmp_ctx, ess_lib) are compile-time constants. raise_site* are unsafe fns, so a safe caller cannot invoke them.
raise_site_closure.discrepancy: raise_site is 3939 call sites, not 3940: the receipt's figure equals the raw match count including the definition line. Off-by-one in reporting; the closure remains static and complete.

neo_dispositions.basis: take_data returns only NULL or a caller-owned seam block (copy for borrowed data); the C probe, the Rust adapter-sequence test and both negative controls reproduce.
finish_data releases a zero-extent MALLOCED block instead of storing an extent; the nonzero size<=extent change remains an external C ABI obligation and is retained.

The destination of save/save_to_mark must be an OSSL_ERR_STATE_new/save object or carry exclusively owned seam slots. A forged ERR_STATE is C-invalid and outside the ABI; the public #[repr(C)] layout offers no ABI-compatible provenance tag. Obligation is retained and enumerated.

neo_dispositions.disposition: ACCEPTED EXTERNAL ABI CONTRACT + cheap validation (retained)
neo_dispositions.basis: out-of-range ring indices are now treated as empty; source extent/NUL termination/no-concurrent-mutation remain the caller's contract for a C-valid saved state. Retained.

ERR_error_string is `pub unsafe extern "C" fn`; its # Safety now requires external serialization for the NULL-buffer form and states the valid-until-next-call lifetime. No safe-Rust caller can reach the data race without unsafe. C consumers must serialize.

CRYPTO_malloc/zalloc/calloc/malloc_array are unsafe extern fns with the NULL-or-NUL-terminated contract; C symbols and signatures are unchanged. But safe in-crate helpers still accept raw `file` and forward it: e.g. src/asn1/owned.rs OwnedBlock::malloc/zalloc are `pub(crate) fn`, src/ml_kem/key.rs and src/provider/mac_legacy_kmgmt.rs OwnedBuf::new families are safe fns. A safe caller can pass a fabricated pointer and trigger c_strlen on the allocation-failure path. The safe-interface gap is therefore not closed.

with_state acquires a thread-local Cell<bool> guard before touching state or loading strings; nested access returns None without forming a second &mut; Drop resets on unwind. Unit test plus Miri SB/TB, ASan and TSan pass. A real CRYPTO_set_mem_functions hook harness was not run; retained BOUNDARY obligation.

helper_file_forwards.independent_finding: The receipt does not enumerate the 24. I verified the class and representative sites. They are safe fns with an unconstrained `file: *const c_char` that reaches the unsafe allocator, so they retain a caller obligation not expressed in the signature.
helper_file_forwards.feasible_repair: src/runtime/mem_coords.rs SeamFile already exists and is used by OwnedBuf/OwnedStr. The raw-parameter helpers can take SeamFile (or become unsafe with a # Safety clause) without any C ABI change.
helper_file_forwards.disposition: RETAINED OBLIGATION / DISCHARGE BLOCKER; not a consumer blocker for the C-only ERR path.

retained_obligations: NEO-ERR-6 residual: 24 (author count) safe helper forwards of a raw `file` parameter; migrate to SeamFile or make unsafe with a contract.
NEO-ERR-2: a nonzero err_data_size greater than the block extent is trusted; external caller contract.
NEO-ERR-3: OSSL_ERR_STATE_save/save_to_mark destination provenance is an external object contract.
NEO-ERR-4: OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore source extent/NUL termination/no concurrent mutation is an external object contract; ring indices are validated.
NEO-ERR-7: no real C allocator-hook reentrancy harness; direct unit test and sanitizers cover the guard path.
R-ERR-1: thread-local ErrState has no Drop; per-thread buffers are not released at thread exit (authority parity, resource residual).
R-ERR-9: the C probe is a court source built manually, not part of cargo test.
Compatibility courts, full library tests and clippy were not re-run in this review; only the controls requested for adjudication were reproduced.
